findings.title: stellar-etl's token transfer export halts on ledgers whose transaction meta is below version 4
findings.reason: intended for the data stellar-etl reads: the public ledger lake holds history re-emitted by a current core, so every ledger there carries TransactionMeta v4, which unified events need. Only locally recorded chains below protocol 23 hold v2 or v3 meta
findings.cause: export_token_transfer builds the processor with NewEventsProcessorForUnifiedEvents (internal/transform/token_transfer.go L15 at 7e3fc9af), which reads the CAP-67 unified events stream and returns "expected version 4 got N" for any other meta version (go-stellar-sdk processors/token_transfer/token_transfer_processor.go L474-L478 at v0.9.0, the version stellar-etl pins). The command exits 1, the adapter retries it, and the harness stops the chain at its first ledger with a transaction: every entry of the five corpus chains recorded at protocols 9 to 22 (meta v2 or v3), and of the 20 explorer chains below protocol 23 recorded with classic events and their backfill off, is not evaluated, on both networks.

findings.title: question: the effects table has no trustline_created for a trustline a Stellar asset contract trust() call opens
findings.cause: transformEffects derives the effects of an InvokeHostFunction operation only from Stellar asset contract events (addInvokeHostFunctionEffects, internal/transform/effects.go L1326-L1440 at 7e3fc9af), which turn transfer, mint, clawback and burn into credit and debit effects. A trustline the contract's trust() function opens (CAP-73) changes the ledger without such an event, so it gets no trustline_created effect, while a ChangeTrust operation that opens the same trustline does (addChangeTrustEffects, L647-L705). The source does not say whether this is intended.

findings.title: question: horizon.Offer reads an offer id given as "+16" or "-0"
findings.cause: horizon.Offer.ID is an int64 tagged `json:"id,string"`, so encoding/json unquotes the text and passes it to strconv.ParseInt, which takes an optional sign: "+16" reads as 16 and "-0" as 0, on every tested version (v0.7.1 to v0.9.0). The field reads horizon's own responses, which carry the canonical text, so the draft is a question. rs-stellar-xdr reads the same two strings the same way (RS-1, rs-stellar-xdr#627); the code is separate, so this is its own finding with RS-1 related.

findings.title: XDR decoders accept arrays, strings and opaque values longer than the schema allows
findings.cause: The generated decoders read a variable-length array, string or opaque with XdrDataInputStream.readArrayLength or readBytes, which bound the count only by the bytes left in the input (lib/src/xdr/xdr_data_io.dart L380-L394), and never check the maximum the schema declares: XdrSCSpecFunctionV0 reads `outputs<1>` with no bound (lib/src/xdr/xdr_sc_spec_function_v0.dart L63), XdrPreconditionsV2 reads `extraSigners<2>` the same way (lib/src/xdr/xdr_preconditions_v2.dart L102). 3.12.0 reads 101 operations, 21 signatures, a 29-byte text memo, a 33-byte symbol, a 65-byte data value, payload and signature, 6 path assets, 11 claimants, 3 extra signers and 2 spec outputs, all of which stellar-core refuses.

findings.title: XDR decoders read Soroban values and authorization trees nested deeper than stellar-core accepts
findings.cause: XdrDataInputStream counts only recursive type decodes, up to maxXdrDecodeDepth (500), and nested delegate signatures, up to maxRecursiveDecodeDepth (128) (lib/src/xdr/xdr_data_io.dart L316-L340). Neither is stellar-core's limit, which counts every nested type, so ScVal maps and vectors and SorobanAuthorizedInvocation trees past core's limit decode and the sdk reads envelopes core refuses; in the other direction, the candidate lane's ledgers with claim predicates, quorum sets or delegate signatures nested to core's ledger limit are refused. The same class as JS-DEPTH in js-stellar-sdk; separate code.

findings.title: stellar xdr decode allocates what a length prefix asks before reading it, so 12 bytes make it abort
findings.cause: stellar xdr decode is stellar-xdr's cli (stellar-xdr 30.0.0 src/cli/decode.rs L78-L100), which reads every input under Limits::none(): no length limit, so a variable-length opaque whose prefix is 0xffffffff is allocated in full before its bytes are read. Under a 4 GiB address space the process aborts (memory allocation of 4294967295 bytes failed, SIGABRT); without a limit it allocates 4 GiB for a 12-byte input before refusing it.

findings.cause: AbstractTransaction.fromEnvelopeXdr(..).hash(network) rebuilds every operation before hashing.
